sources.quote: hairstyling is a compulsory trade in Ontario and Skilled Trades Ontario keeps a public register of certificate holders
sources.title: Hairstylist - Skilled Trades Ontario
sources.evidence: Hairstylist is a compulsory trade in Ontario. To legally practice this trade, you need to hold a Registered Training Agreement, Provisional Certificate of Qualification or Certificate of Qualification and appear on Skilled Trades Ontario's Public Register.

sources.quote: charges a one off commission of about 20 percent on the first appointment of a client who arrives through its marketplace
sources.title: Marketplace new client fees on Fresha
sources.evidence: Fresha only charges a one-time 20% commission on the very first appointment made by a new client who discovers you through the Marketplace. Returning clients who rebook with you are not charged Marketplace commission.

sources.quote: TikTok was ordered by the federal government in late 2024 to wind down its Canadian corporate operations
sources.publisher: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
sources.title: Government of Canada orders the wind up of TikTok Technology Canada, Inc. following a national security review under the Investment Canada Act - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: On November 6, 2024, the Government of Canada ordered the wind up of the Canadian business carried on by TikTok Technology Canada, Inc., following a multi-step national security review process under the Investment Canada Act. The government clarified that it was not blocking Canadians' access to the TikTok application or their ability to create content.

sources.quote: Gifted collaborations must be disclosed under Competition Bureau influencer guidance
sources.title: Influencer marketing and the Competition Act
sources.evidence: Influencers should disclose all material connections they have with the business, product or service they are promoting. A connection could be getting paid or receiving commissions, free products or services, or discounts, in exchange for promoting a business, product or service. Disclosures should be prominent and visible on all devices without having to click or tap to expand the post.

sources.quote: francisation registration with the Office québécois de la langue française starts at 25 employees
sources.title: Démarche de francisation - Les entreprises employant de 25 à 49 personnes sont invitées à s'inscrire à l'Office québécois de la langue française sans attendre
sources.evidence: À compter du 1er juin 2025, l'obligation de s'inscrire à l'Office québécois de la langue française afin d'entreprendre une démarche de francisation s'étend aux entreprises de 25 à 49 personnes. Businesses that employ 25 people or more in Quebec during a 6-month period have the obligation to register with the Office to begin a francisation process.

sources.quote: several treat a voucher for one named service differently
sources.title: Buying or using gift cards
sources.evidence: Gift cards from retail businesses and gift cards from malls are covered under the Consumer Protection Act. Gift cards for one specific service (such as a gift certificate for a massage at a spa) may come with an expiry date and lose their value if not used.

sources.quote: the CRA treats the shop owner as the employer for employment insurance even when the worker rents the chair
sources.title: Payments and earnings related to barbers and hairdressers - Calculate payroll deductions and contributions - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: For EI purposes, as the owner or operator of an establishment that offers barbering and hairdressing services, you may be considered an employer of the self-employed barber and hairdresser, even if you do not provide a payment to them. When a barber or hairdresser enters into an agreement as a chair renter, the owner or operator of the establishment is deemed to be the employer and is responsible for paying the employee's and the employer's share of the EI premiums.

flags.quote: TikTok was ordered by the federal government in late 2024 to wind down its Canadian corporate operations
flags.issue: Outdated. On March 9, 2026, Minister Joly announced that the Government of Canada completed a further national security review of TikTok Technology Canada Inc. under the Investment Canada Act and decided to permit the investment to proceed, subject to new legally binding undertakings, superseding the November 2024 wind-up order.
